question: Does a low training cost always mean a good model?
direct_answer: No; it can still overfit and generalize poorly.
expanded_answer: A model can achieve a very low cost on the training set by fitting noise or idiosyncrasies in that data. Good performance usually depends on both the training objective and how well the model generalizes to unseen examples.
key_points: Low training cost does not guarantee generalization
common_wrong_ideas: If the cost is low, the model must be good
Training cost and generalization are the same thing
